channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Molly Meldrum Dies at 83, the Australian Music Legend Who Championed a Nation's Sound
item.description: Ian "Molly" Meldrum, the Australian music critic and broadcaster who presented the television show Countdown for 13 years and spent six decades championing homegrown music, has died at the age of 83, his family has announced.

item.title: Alcaraz Beats Zverev to Win First ATP Finals Title in Turin
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6(7) in Turin on Sunday to win the ATP Finals for the first time, ending a season in which he also became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam.

item.title: Skubal Agrees Record $450 Million Mets Deal, the Richest Ever for a Pitcher
item.description: Tarik Skubal has agreed a nine-year deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets, the biggest contract ever given to a pitcher, ending one of the most closely watched free-agent races in years.

item.title: Iran's Guards Claim Supertanker Sank After Mine Strikes in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers struck naval mines on an unauthorised route in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, and claim one of them, a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil, sank. There is no independent confirmation of the sinking.

item.title: Fire Sweeps Through Six Hotels in Zanzibar's Nungwi as 183 Tourists Are Evacuated
item.description: A fire tore through six hotels and dozens of shops in Nungwi, one of Zanzibar's most popular beach resorts, on Saturday afternoon, forcing the evacuation of 183 tourists. No deaths were reported, though some hotel staff sustained minor injuries during the evacuation.

item.title: Democrats Clinch 258 House Seats, Their Largest Majority Since 1992
item.description: Democrats have secured at least 258 seats in the United States House of Representatives, giving the party its largest majority in the chamber since 1992 and a sweeping mandate from a midterm election fought largely on the cost of living.

item.title: US Intelligence Chief Warns More Tech Outages Are Coming as Ageing Systems Are Upgraded
item.description: The United States' top intelligence official has warned Americans to expect further technology outages and service disruptions as companies and government agencies replace ageing computer systems, saying interruptions are an inevitable part of the upgrade process.

item.title: Marquez Seals Record-Equalling Eighth MotoGP Title With Eighth Place in Portugal
item.description: Marc Marquez won the 2026 MotoGP world championship on Sunday, finishing eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix to seal a record-equalling eighth premier-class title with one round still to run.

item.title: Delta Restores Weight-and-Balance System After More Than 1,600 Flights Delayed
item.description: Delta Air Lines said on Sunday afternoon that the automated system that calculates aircraft weight and balance was working again, after a failure in the system delayed more than 1,600 flights, about half the airline's mainline schedule, at the start of the Thanksgiving travel rush.

item.title: Satellite Images Show Russian Corvette Mostly Sunk After Benghazi Drone Strike
item.description: Satellite images show a Russian navy corvette has mostly capsized and sunk at Benghazi port in eastern Libya after a sea-drone strike on Sunday, as a second attack hit a Malta-flagged merchant vessel off the coast.

item.title: Settlers Torch Cars and Spray Racist Graffiti in Overnight Attacks on West Bank Villages
item.description: Israeli settlers torched cars and vandalised homes in several Palestinian villages across the occupied West Bank overnight, residents said, in attacks that a leading rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned as 'Jewish terrorism'.

item.title: Centrica Boss Warns Energy Bill Non-Payment Will Worsen as January Rise Nears
item.description: The boss of British Gas owner Centrica has said he is hugely concerned about the impact of January's expected energy bill rise, warning that more households will stop paying and that the cost is already being spread across every electricity customer.

item.title: Six Wounded in Strike on Sanaa Oil Company Fuel Station as Saudi Defences Down Drone and Missile
item.description: Six workers were wounded when a strike hit a fuel station run by Yemen's state oil company in the capital Sanaa early on Sunday, Houthi-run health authorities said, as Saudi air defences reported downing a Houthi drone and a ballistic missile.

item.title: Four Reported Killed as Drones Strike Homes in Khartoum Overnight
item.description: Drones struck residential areas in and around Sudan's capital Khartoum early on Sunday, killing four people, including a child, medical sources and a rights group said, and damaging a United Nations premises with staff inside.

item.title: Messi Escapes Red Card After Throwing Ball at Opponent as Inter Miami Crash 3-0 to Columbus
item.description: Lionel Messi escaped a red card after throwing the ball into an opponent's face as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat against Columbus Crew in the opening match of their MLS Cup playoff series on Saturday.

item.title: Six Killed in Dymer Drone Strike as Boy Is Pulled Alive From Rubble After 14 Hours
item.description: Rescue workers have pulled a seven-year-old boy alive from the ruins of a five-storey apartment building in Dymer after nearly 14 hours under the rubble, as the death toll from the overnight Russian drone strike climbed to at least six.

item.title: South Korea Education Minister Resigns Over AI Cheating Scandal That Shook College Entrance Exam
item.description: South Korea's education minister has resigned after a cheating scandal involving artificial intelligence overshadowed the country's most important exam, with the president accepting his resignation on the same day.

item.title: Trump's Iran Strategy Splits His Team as Blockade Enters Its 130th Day
item.description: Donald Trump has settled for now on squeezing Iran's economy rather than returning to full-scale war, a middle course that has exposed a split inside his own team over whether the blockade or a deal is the way out.

item.title: Dashcam Captures Missile Slamming Into Lviv Street as Two Killed in Russian Barrage
item.description: Dashcam footage has captured the moment a Russian projectile slammed into a building on a street in Lviv, in western Ukraine, during a missile and drone barrage on Friday that killed two people and injured at least 10.

item.title: Verstappen Takes Wild Las Vegas Win as Late Mercedes Drama Hands McLaren a Double Podium
item.description: Max Verstappen won a thrilling Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday, surviving a night-long battle with both Mercedes cars before late trouble for the Silver Arrows handed McLaren a double podium, for his third win on the streets of Nevada in four years.

item.title: Paolo Bulgari Dies at 89, the Jeweller Who Turned a Family Business Into a Global Luxury House
item.description: Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who turned a small family jewellery business into one of the world's great luxury houses, has died at the age of 89, his family has announced.

item.title: Turkey Warns Iran War's Economic Burden Is Turning Destructive and Urges a US-Iran Deal
item.description: Turkey's foreign minister has warned that the economic fallout from the war on Iran is growing heavier for countries around the world, saying a deal between Washington and Tehran is needed to ease the strain and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: 24 Body Bags Removed From Indonesia Candy Factory as Search Resumes After Fire
item.description: Indonesian police have removed 24 body bags from a candy factory destroyed by fire in western Java, as the search for dozens of missing workers resumes on Monday after being suspended overnight.

item.title: China Warns of Countermeasures After US Bars Its Telecom Firms From American Phone Numbers
item.description: China's commerce ministry said on Sunday it firmly opposes the US regulator's vote to bar Chinese telecom firms from direct access to American phone numbers, warning Beijing will take necessary countermeasures if the ban goes ahead.

item.title: US Court Sends Summonses for India's Ajit Doval to Delhi Courts in Pannun Assassination Lawsuit
item.description: A federal court in New York has sent legal summonses for India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former intelligence chief Samant Goel to three district courts in Delhi, asking them to help deliver the papers in a civil lawsuit that accuses Indian officials of plotting to kill a Sikh separatist leader in the United States.

item.title: Eisenkot Invites Netanyahu's Likud to Marathon Coalition Talks in Bid to Form Broad Government
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief tasked with forming Israel's next government, has invited Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party to marathon coalition talks starting on Sunday, in the clearest sign yet that he is trying to build a broad government that leaves Netanyahu out of the top job.

item.title: Turnout Falls as France Protests Enter Sixth Weekend, With Clashes in Marseille and Lyon
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched across France on Saturday for a sixth straight weekend of protests over the cost of living and public services, but turnout fell sharply from a week earlier as about 70,000 police officers were deployed and sporadic clashes broke out in several cities.

item.title: Trump Vows a Permanent Iran Deal That No Future President Can Undo
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he intends to secure a permanent agreement with Iran that would prevent Tehran from ever obtaining a nuclear weapon, and that no future American president should be able to reverse it.

item.title: Aoun Demands Israeli Withdrawal and an End to Iranian Meddling in Lebanon
item.description: Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun said on Saturday that his country cannot fully celebrate its independence while Israeli forces hold Lebanese land and foreign powers interfere in its affairs, in a speech that pressed both Israel to withdraw and Hezbollah to give up its weapons.

item.title: Pezeshkian Says Iran Faces 'Silent Economic War' Tougher Than Missile War
item.description: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday that his country is fighting a 'silent economic war' that is far more difficult than a military conflict, as the war with the United States and Israel squeezes its economy.
